To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first step of folate biosynthesis is catalyzed by a Zn2+-independent enzyme in many bacteria, and that this enzyme is activated by a variety or divalent metals.
we discovered a previously unknown Zn2+-independent GTP cyclohydrolyase (GCYH) enzyme, GCYHB, that is present in ∽25% of prokaryotes.

the GCYH-I enzymes from B. subtilis are functionally redundant but differentially regulated, that the Zn2+-dependent GCYH-1A is a homodecameric enzyme that belongs to the T-fold super family, and that the Zn2-independent GCYH- IB is a homotetramer that belongs to the same super family but exhibits significant differences in structure and active-site organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular basis of Zn2+-dependent folate biosynthesis in Bacteria and plants and the identification of new Zn2+ and GTP-independent pathways for folate biosynthesis.
the discovery and characterization of a novel GCYH-I that has been overlooked for decades and is widespread among bacteria and Archaea.
understanding the mechanisms by which organisms synthesize folates, a family of cofactors with critical roles in human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GCYH-I is a Zn-dependent enzyme, but the Zn2+ ion is not absolutely required, and the Zn2+ dependence is not a conserved property of this enzyme.
GCYH-I is a zinc-dependent enzyme, and GCYH-Ib is a non-zinc-dependent enzyme.
the GCYH family of enzymes is a highly diverse and mechanistically plastic group of enzymes, with the GCYH-B family being the most diverse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a new GCYH enzyme in the T-fold family and showed that it is activated by different metals and has a different structure than the canonical GCYHB enzyme.
the GCYH-I enzyme is an ancient enzyme that has evolved multiple times in bacteria, plants and mammals, and has been adapted for use in different biosynthetic pathways.
GCYH-I is a Zn2+-dependent GTP cyclohydrolyase that catalyzes a key step in the de novo folyl pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GCYH family of enzymes is much more diverse than previously recognized.
GCYH-I is a metalloenzyme with a broad range of metal dependencies.

the Zn2+-dependent GCYH-1A enzyme is present in all organisms that synthesize folate and that the newly discovered Zn2+-independent GCYH-B enzymes are present only in prokaryotic organisms and are likely to be important for folate biosynthesis when zinc is limiting.
